messages:
anika: Heads up — since yesterday afternoon we've seen repeated tail-latency spikes on the shared GPU pool in eu-west-1. Correlates with one tenant running lots of long batch jobs. Any quick mitigations?

kevin: Saw that too. GPU util stays high but sched queue depth climbs and preemptions spike. Likely a noisy neighbor holding contexts. Quick win = per-tenant concurrent slot cap + token-bucket at ingress. @maria thoughts? :thinking_face: 

maria: We have per-tenant qps limits but those don't help when a job holds a GPU for minutes. Need active-concurrency caps (active contexts) rather than request-rate only.

ryan: Agreed. Proposal: admission control middleware that enforces active_gpu_contexts per tenant with (min_guarantee, max_active, burst). On overload, two options: enqueue with timeout OR return 429 + Retry-After. For shared pool I'd prefer 429 for latency-sensitive tenants; enqueue for Reserved/Dedicated tenants.

anika: +1. For public/shared pool, returning 429 is safer to avoid huge queueing delays and unpredictable GPU cost. We should validate impact with metrics first.

kevin: Metrics to add before any rollout: active_gpu_contexts{tenant}, queue_length{tenant}, rejection_rate{tenant}, p50/p95/p99_latency_by_tenant, and % of pool owned by top-1/top-3 tenants. Alert if one tenant > 40% active contexts for 5m.

maria: Prototype admission config snippet (very small, for discussion):
```yaml
# admission policy (example)
policies:
  - scope: shared_gpu_pool
    tenant: "*"
    min_guarantee: 1           # soft slot guarantee per tenant
    max_active: 8             # hard concurrent contexts
    burst: 2                  # temporary burst allowance
    action_on_exceed: reject  # reject vs queue
    queue_timeout_ms: 3000    # if action_on_exceed == queue
```

ryan: Also consider soft-preemption: when overall pool >= 90% start signaling low-priority batch tasks to checkpoint/stop and free contexts. Evict politely rather than hard kill.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled to eng-sre canary group in ~30m (will post status).

anika: Plan for next steps: 1) instrument metrics (kevin) 2) marriage of middleware + config (maria + ryan) 3) canary on eng-sre -> 5% traffic in us-west -> monitor 6) expand to 20% then full for shared pool if stable. I'll open the ticket and link here.

kevin: Note on cost tradeoffs: enqueuing increases GPU walltime and billable hours; rejecting shifts burden to customers (retries/backoff). We'll surface cost estimates in the ticket so PMs can decide default behavior per tenancy (shared vs dedicated).

maria: I'll prototype admission middleware today and push a small PR for review, include unit tests + a k6 load test scenario.

anika: Great — thanks. If the canary goes green we'll wire up automatic alerts for top-tenant domination and start enforcing max_active after a 24h observation window.

ryan: One extra ask: add tenant label to existing GPU context traces so we can correlate p99 with stack traces. That saved us last time.

anika: Yup adding that to the metrics ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
